record.title: Extrapolate azimuth angles: Text and edge guided ISAR image generation based on foundation model
record.abstract: Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) has been widely applied in remote sensing and space target monitoring. Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) based on ISAR imagery plays a critical role in target interpretation and pose estimation. With the growing adoption of intelligent methods in the ATR domain, the quantity and quality of ISAR data have become decisive factors influencing algorithm performance. However, due to the complexity of ISAR imaging algorithms and the high cost of data acquisition, high-quality ISAR image datasets remain extremely scarce. As a result, learning the underlying characteristics of existing ISAR data to generate large-scale usable samples has become a pressing research focus. Although some preliminary studies have explored ISAR image data augmentation, most of them rely on image sequence interpolation or conditional generation, both of which exhibit critical limitations: the former requires densely sampled image sequences with small angular intervals, while the latter can only model the mapping between limited azimuth conditions and ISAR images. Neither approach is capable of generating images of new targets under unseen azimuth conditions, resulting in poor generalization and leaving substantial room for further exploration. To address these limitations, we formally define a novel research problem, termed ISAR azimuth angle extrapolation. This task fundamentally involves high-dimensional, structured, cross-view image synthesis, requiring the restoration of visual details while ensuring physical consistency and structural stability. To address this problem, we propose ISAR-ExtraNet, a foundation-model-based framework for ISAR azimuth angle extrapolation. ISAR-ExtraNet leverages the strong representation, modeling, and generalization capabilities of pretrained foundation models to generate ISAR images of new targets under novel azimuth conditions. Specifically, the model employs a two-stage coarse-to-fine fine-tuning strategy, incorporating optical image contours and scattering center distribution constraints to guide the generation process. This design enhances both semantic alignment and structural fidelity in the generated ISAR images. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ISAR-ExtraNet significantly outperforms baseline methods and fine-tuned foundation models, achieving 28.76 dB in PSNR and 0.80 in SSIM. We hope that the training paradigm introduced in ISAR-ExtraNet will inspire further exploration of the ISAR azimuth extrapolation problem and foster progress in this emerging research area.

record.title: Mamba-CNN hybrid Multi-scale ship detection Network driven by a Dual-perception feature of Doppler and Scattering
record.abstract: Ship detection is crucial for both military and civilian applications and is a key use of polarimetric SAR (PolSAR). While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) enhance PolSAR ship detection with powerful feature extraction, existing approaches still face challenges in discriminating targets from clutter, detecting multi-scale objects in complex scenes, and achieving real-time detection. To address these issues, we propose a Mamba-CNN hybrid Multi-scale ship detection Network driven by a Dual-perception feature of Doppler and Scattering. First, at the input feature level, a Dual-perception feature of Doppler and Scattering (DDS) is introduced, effectively differentiating ship and clutter pixels to enhance the network’s ship discrimination. Specifically, Doppler characteristics distinguish between moving and stationary targets, while scattering characteristics reveal fundamental differences between targets and clutter. Second, at the network architecture level, a Mamba-CNN hybrid Multi-scale ship detection Network (MCMN) is designed to improve multi-scale ship detection in complex scenarios. It uses a Multi-scale Information Perception Module (MIPM) to adaptively aggregate multi-scale features and a Local-Global Feature Enhancement Module (LGFEM) based on Mamba for long-range context modeling. MCMN remains efficient through feature grouping, pointwise and depthwise convolutions, meeting real-time requirements. Finally, extensive experiments on the GF-3 and SSDD datasets demonstrate the superiority of DDS and MCMN. DDS effectively distinguishes ships from clutter across scenarios. As an input feature, it boosts average F1-score and AP by 4.3% and 4.3%, respectively, over HV intensity, and outperforms other polarization features. MCMN achieves state-of-the-art results, improving AP by 1.2% and 0.8% on the two datasets while reducing parameters by 1.29M, FLOPs by 1.5G, and inference time by 59.2%.

record.title: Complex convolutional sparse coding InSAR phase filtering Incorporating directional gradients and second-order difference regularization
record.abstract: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) is a technology that can effectively obtain ground information, conduct large-scale topography mapping, and monitor surface deformation. However, InSAR data is interfered by speckle noise caused by radar echo signal fading, ground background clutter, and decoherence, which affects the InSAR interferometric phase quality and thus reduces the accuracy of InSAR results. The existing Complex Convolutional Sparse Coding Gradient Regularization (ComCSC-GR) method incorporates gradient regularization by considering the sparse coefficient matrix’s gradients in both row (azimuth) and column (range) directions. It is an advanced and effective interferogram phase filtering method that can improve the interferogram quality. However, this method does not take into account the variation characteristics of the diagonal gradient and the second-order difference information (caused by edge mutations). As a result, the interferogram still exhibits problems such as staircase artifacts in high-noise and low-coherence areas, uneven interferograms (caused by a large number of residual points), and unclear phase edge structure. This article introduces multiple directional gradients and second-order differential Laplacian operator information, and construct two models: “Complex Convolutional Sparse Coding Model with L2-norm Regularization of Directional Gradients and Laplacian Operator (ComCSC-RCDL) ” and “Complex Convolutional Sparse Coding Model Coupled with L1-norm Total Variation Regularization (ComCSC-RCDL-TV)”. These methods enhance the fidelity of phase texture and edge structure, and improve the quality of InSAR interferogram filtering phase in low-coherence scenarios. Comparative experiments were conducted using simulated data, real data from Sentinel-1 and LuTan-1 (LT-1), and advanced methods including ComCSC-GR and InSAR-BM3D (real data experiments included comparison experiments before and after removing the interferogram orbit error). The results show that the proposed model method performs better than the comparative model, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed model.

record.title: Beyond the surface: machine learning uncovers ENSO’s hidden and contrasting impacts on phytoplankton vertical structure
record.abstract: Satellite-based ocean remote sensing is fundamentally limited to observing the ocean surface (top-of-the-ocean), a constraint that severely hinders a comprehensive understanding of how the entire water column ecosystem responds to climate variability like the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Surface-only views cannot resolve critical shifts in the subsurface chlorophyll maximum (SCM), a key layer for marine biodiversity and biogeochemical cycles. To overcome this critical limitation, we develop and validate a novel stacked generalization ensemble machine learning framework. This framework robustly reconstructs a 25-year (1998–2022) high-resolution 3D chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) field by integrating 133,792 globally distributed Biogeochemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) profiles with multi-source satellite data. The reconstructed 3D Chl-a fields were rigorously validated against both satellite and in-situ observations, achieving strong agreement (R ≥ 0.97, mean absolute percentage error ≤ 27 %), demonstrating the robustness and reliability of the framework. Applying this framework to two contrasting South China Sea upwelling system reveals that ENSO phases fundamentally restructure the entire water column. Crucially, we discover that El Niño and La Niña exert opposing effects on the SCM: El Niño events deepen and thin the SCM with decreasing Chl-a by 15–30 %, whereas La Niña events cause it to shoal and thicken, increasing Chl-a by 20–40 %. This vertical restructuring is mechanistically linked to ENSO-driven changes in wind stress curl, Rossby wave propagation, and nitrate availability. Furthermore, we identify a significant subsurface-first response, where the SCM reacts to ENSO forcing months before significant changes are detectable at the surface. Our findings demonstrate that a three-dimensional perspective, enabled by our novel remote sensing reconstruction framework, is essential for accurately quantifying the biogeochemical consequences of climate variability, revealing that surface-only observations can significantly underestimate the vulnerability and response of marine ecosystems to ENSO events.

record.title: RECREATE: Supervised contrastive learning and inpainting based hyperspectral image denoising
record.abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) contains information at various spectra, making it valuable in several real-world applications such as environmental monitoring, agriculture, and remote sensing. However, the acquisition process often introduces noise, necessitating effective HSI denoising methods to maintain its applicability. Deep Learning (DL) is considered as the de-facto for HSI denoising, but it requires a significant number of training samples to optimize network parameters for effective denoising outcomes. However, obtaining extensive datasets is challenging in HSI, leading to epistemic uncertainties and thereby deteriorating the denoising performance. This paper introduces a novel supervised contrastive learning (SCL) method, RECREATE, to enhance feature learning and mitigate the issue of epistemic uncertainty for HSI denoising. Furthermore, we introduce the exploration of image inpainting as an auxiliary task to enhance the HSI denoising performance. By adding HSI inpainting to CL, our method essentially enhances HSI denoising by increasing training datasets and enforcing improved feature learning. Experimental outcomes on various HSI datasets validate the efficacy of RECREATE, showcasing its potential for integration with existing HSI denoising techniques to enhance their performance, both qualitatively and quantitatively. This innovative method holds promise for addressing the limitations posed by limited training data and thereby advancing the field toward proposing better HSI denoising methods.

record.title: AMS-Former: Adaptive multi-scale transformer for multi-modal image matching
record.abstract: Multi-modal image (MMI) matching plays a crucial role in the fusion of multi-source image information. However, due to the significant geometric and modality differences in MMI, existing methods often fail to achieve satisfactory matching performance. To address these challenges, we propose an end-to-end MMI matching approach, named adaptive multi-scale transformer (AMS-Former). First, AMS-Former constructs a multi-scale image matching framework that integrates contextual information across different scales, effectively identifying potential corresponding points and thereby improving matching accuracy. To handle the challenges caused by modality differences, we design a cross-modal feature extraction module with an adaptive modulation strategy. This module effectively couples features from different modalities, enhancing feature representation and improving model robustness under complex modality differences. To further enhance matching performance, we design a suitable loss function for the proposed AMS-Former to guide the optimization of network parameters. Finally, we use a cross-scale mutual supervision strategy to remove incorrect corresponding points and enhance the reliability of the matching results. Extensive experiments on five MMI datasets demonstrate that AMS-Former outperforms state-of-the-art methods, including RIFT, ASS, COFSM, POS-GIFT, Matchformer, SEMLA, TopicFM, and Lightglue. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Henryrjh/AMS_Former.

record.title: A weakly supervised approach for large-scale agricultural parcel extraction from VHR imagery via foundation models and adaptive noise correction
record.abstract: Large-scale and fine-grained extraction of agricultural parcels from very-high-resolution (VHR) imagery is essential for precision agriculture. However, traditional parcel segmentation methods and fully supervised deep learning approaches typically face scalability constraints due to costly manual annotations, while extraction accuracy is generally limited by the inadequate capacity of segmentation architectures to represent complex agricultural scenes. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Weakly Supervised approach for agricultural Parcel Extraction (WSPE), which leverages publicly available 10 m resolution images and labels to guide the delineation of 0.5 m agricultural parcels. The WSPE framework integrates the tabular (Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network, TabPFN) and the vision foundation model (Segment Anything Model 2, SAM2) to initially generate pseudo-labels with high geometric precision. These pseudo-labels are further refined for semantic accuracy through an adaptive noisy label correction module based on curriculum learning. The refined knowledge is distilled into the proposed Triple-branch Kolmogorov-Arnold enhanced Boundary-aware Network (TKBNet), a prompt-free end-to-end architecture enabling rapid inference and scalable deployment, with outputs vectorized through post-processing. The effectiveness of WSPE was evaluated on a self-constructed dataset from nine agricultural zones in China, the public AI4Boundaries and FGFD datasets, and three large-scale regions: Zhoukou, Hengshui, and Fengcheng. Results demonstrate that WSPE and its integrated TKBNet achieve robust performance across datasets with diverse agricultural scenes, validated by extensive comparative and ablation experiments. The weakly supervised approach achieves 97.7 % of fully supervised performance, and large-scale deployment verifies its scalability and generalization, offering a practical solution for fine-grained, large-scale agricultural parcel mapping. Code is available at https://github.com/zhaowenpeng/WSPE.

record.title: Satellite-based heat Index estimatioN modEl (SHINE): An integrated machine learning approach for the conterminous United States
record.abstract: The accelerating frequency, duration and intensity of extreme heat events demand accurate, spatially complete heat exposure metrics. Here, a modeling approach is presented for estimating the daily-maximum Heat Index (HI) at 1 km spatial resolution. Our study area covered the conterminous United States (CONUS) during the warm season (May to September) between 2003 and 2023. More than 4.6 million observations from approximately 2000 weather stations were paired with weather-related, geographical, land cover and historical climatic factors to develop the proposed Satellite-based Heat Index estimatioN modEl (SHINE). Selected explanatory variables at daily temporal intervals included reanalysis products from Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications (MERRA) and direct satellite products from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) sensor. The most influential variables for HI estimation were the MERRA surface layer height and specific humidity products and the dual-pass MODIS daily land surface temperatures. These were followed by land cover products capturing water and forest presence, historical norms of wind speed and maximum temperature, elevation information and the corresponding day of year. An Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regressor trained with spatial cross-validation explained 93 % of the variance (R2 = 0.93) and attained a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.9°C and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.4°C. Comparison of alternative configurations showed that while a MERRA-only model provided slightly higher accuracy (RMSE of 1.8°C), its coarse resolution failed to capture fine-scale heat variations. Conversely, a MODIS-only model offered kilometer-scale spatial resolution but with higher estimation errors (RMSE of 2.9°C). Integrating both MERRA and MODIS sources enabled SHINE to maintain spatial detail and preserved accuracy, underscoring the complementary strengths of reanalysis and satellite products. SHINE also demonstrated resistance to missing MODIS LST observations due to clouds as the additional RMSE error was approximately 0.5°C in the worst case of missing both morning and afternoon MODIS land surface temperature observations. Spatial error analysis revealed <1.7°C RMSE in arid and Mediterranean zones but larger, more heterogeneous errors in the humid Midwest and High Plains. From the policy perspective and considering the HI operational range for public-health heat effects, the proposed SHINE approach outperformed typically used proxies, such as land surface and air temperature. The resulting 1 km daily HI estimations can potentially be used as the foundation of the first wall-to-wall, multi-decadal, high resolution heat dataset for CONUS and offer actionable information for public-health heat studies, energy-demand forecasting and environmental-justice implications.

record.title: Comparative assessment of AI-based and classical DSAS approaches in multi-temporal shoreline prediction: A case study of Ras El-Bar coast, Egypt
record.abstract: Along Ras El-Bar coast, NE Nile Delta of Egypt, intense human interventions and natural processes give rise to highly distinctive non-linear shoreline dynamics that challenge the stationarity assumptions of traditional forecasting. Classical methods, specifically the Digital Shoreline Analysis System Linear Regression Rate (DSAS-LRR), often fail to capture abrupt anthropogenic regime shifts induced by engineering structures. This study presents a comparative assessment of DSAS-LRR against two artificial intelligence (AI) recurrent neural networks, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Nonlinear Autoregressive Exogenous (NARX), using a multi-decadal satellite-derived shoreline record (1982–2024) to project shoreline evolution through 2050. Results show DSAS-LRR unrealistic projections, exceeding 250 m of displacement by 2050, due to its inability to account for rapid anthropogenic interventions. Conversely, AI models successfully captured complex temporal responses. While LSTM provided conservative estimates, the intervention-aware NARX model achieved the highest predictive accuracy and spatial consistency. Model performance was rigorously evaluated via Taylor diagrams, Performance Index Metric (PIm), and transect-based RMSE analysis, and was further validated by an independent 2025 “blind test”. NARX consistently outperformed both models, accurately reproducing accretion in breakwater shadow zones and moderate erosion between structures, with average RMSE values of 6–14 m. These findings underscore that for anthropogenically modified coasts, intervention-aware AI is no longer just an alternative, it is an essential tool for reliable prediction. The proposed framework provides a transferable roadmap for evidence-based coastal management and infrastructure planning in vulnerable deltaic systems worldwide.

record.title: A novel transformer-based CO2 retrieval framework incorporating prior constraint and hierarchical features injection: assessment of transferability for Tansat-2
record.abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2), the primary contributor to global warming, significantly impacts global climate change. Remote sensing is an effective approach for monitoring atmospheric CO2 concentrations. However, the commonly used satellite’s full-physics Optimal Estimation (OE) method is time-consuming and requires advanced equipment. Additionally, traditional deep learning algorithms for satellite CO2 retrieval suffer from limitations in accuracy and an inability to extrapolate effectively to unseen high values, caused by the gradually increasing concentrations over time. Balancing both efficiency and extrapolation capabilities is a critical task, especially for the next generation of large-swath carbon satellite with a significant increase in data volumes, such as Tansat-2. In this study, we first employed the OCO-2 data from 2020 to construct a Transformer-based structure and integrate prior constraint and hierarchical features injection mechanism for high precision CO2 retrieval, and achieved an outstanding result with the R, RMSE, and MAPE of 0.939, 0.746 ppm, and 0.132 %. Based on the model, we evaluated its extrapolation capability using OCO-2 data from 2021 to 2024, demonstrating a robust performance and strong generalization ability (R = 0.938–0.951, RMSE = 1.083–1.310 ppm, MAPE = 0.208–0.256 %). Finally, we assessed the transferability of this model using simulated Tansat-2 data (August 18, 2020), achieving metrics of R = 0.657, RMSE = 1.299 ppm, and MAPE = 0.239 %, indicating the model’s effective transfer capabilities. The proposed model has the potential to provide a feasible solution for rapidly retrieving high-precision CO2, especially for the next generation of large-swath carbon satellites.

record.title: Explainable urban renewal prediction at building-scale using hierarchical graph neural networks
record.abstract: Urban renewal prediction is critical for sustainable development, yet existing methods often overlook complex spatial dependencies and lack explainability. This study proposes an explainable hierarchical graph network for urban renewal (URHGN) prediction. It employs a hierarchical graph to model building and community level spatial interactions with GNNExplainer to predict renewal potential and quantify driving factors. Applied to Beijing, URHGN achieves an F1-score of 0.855 ± 0.012, outperforming traditional machine learning (0.700–0.775) and single-layer graph methods (0.789–0.810). Explainability analysis reveals that building-level features like floor (importance: 0.485 ± 0.030) are primary drivers while community-level context like house price (0.343 ± 0.003) provides essential supplements. Spatial relationships prove more influential than node features, with contribution scores of 0.271 ± 0.019 and 0.124 ± 0.017 respectively. The model identifies 15,990 buildings with very high renewal potential (scores > 0.8), advancing explainable GeoAI (XGeoAI) methodologies for evidence-based urban planning and establishing a foundation for future dynamic models incorporating temporal changes. The code is available at: https://github.com/kkxiaoqin/URHGN.

record.title: Knowledge-data-model-driven multimodal few-shot learning for hyperspectral fine classification: Generalization across sensor, category and scene
record.abstract: Fine-grained land-cover mapping is crucial for accurately assessing environmental degradation and monitoring socioeconomic dynamics. Few-shot learning of hyperspectral images offers a promising solution in cases where sample collection is limited. However, previous studies, such as tree species mapping, typically use 1% or 0.5% of samples per class, yielding thousands of samples for common species but struggling to identify unseen or rare species (only one sample/shot) in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, inevitable cross-sensor, cross-category, and cross-scene variations significantly increase the occurrence of unseen or rare classes and spectral heterogeneity within common land-cover types. To this being, we propose Knowing-Net, a knowledge-data-model-driven multimodal few-shot learning network, to bridge the application gap for fine-grained mapping of unseen or rare classes. In Knowing-Net, prior knowledge of sensor, i.e., spectral parameters, is leveraged to reconstruct cross-sensor hyperspectral images, mitigating heterogeneity in spectral responses across datasets and enabling cross-domain transfer across different sensors, scenes, and land cover types. To breakthrough the gap in recognizing unseen classes, multimodal data, including textual descriptions and natural images of unseen classes, is embedded into network to construct shared side information through modality-specific feature learning. By designing a cross-alignment mechanism for hyperspectral and multimodal information in a shared semantic space, distinct encoders are guided to produce consistent distribution for the same class across different modalities, reducing sample dependency and facilitating the identification of unseen or rare classes. Finally, inspired by the first law of geography, a sliding discriminant window is designed to incorporate spatial context, enhancing geography interpretability and robustness to noise. We evaluate Knowing-Net on five challenging airborne hyperspectral datasets with a fine-grained classification system, covering crop type, tree species, and similar urban land covers with varying materials. Extensive experiments on five datasets consistently demonstrate Knowing-net’s superiority over state-of-the-art methods in both mapping performance and cross-domain generalization. Notably, the unified framework achieves state-of-the-art results in one-shot learning and establishes a new paradigm in zero-shot classification for fine-grained land cover tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive generalization of FSL across sensor, category, and scene for hyperspectral image-based fine mapping.

record.title: Neural network based on high freedom dynamic collaboration of flows for meteorological data temporal downscaling
record.abstract: Temporal refinement of meteorological fields is a critical yet challenging task, as it requires reconstructing physically consistent intermediate states from sparsely sampled observations. Conventional approaches either rely on computationally intensive numerical simulations or exhibit limited generalization when applied to complex atmospheric conditions. Recent advances in deep learning-based frame interpolation offer a data-driven alternative for modeling temporal evolution, providing new opportunities for meteorological time downscaling. This study proposes a deep neural network specifically designed to perform temporal downscaling of multivariate meteorological fields. The model independently estimates spatially adaptive kernel parameters for each variable and location, while dynamically integrating information across multiple meteorological fields. It generates output frames under the guidance of the feature space. Compared with existing approaches, the proposed framework demonstrates enhanced flexibility in capturing complex and heterogeneous atmospheric dynamics. Experiments conducted on 2 m temperature, surface pressure, specific humidity at 1000 hPa, and total precipitation demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy, robustness, computational efficiency, strong scalability and transferability.

record.title: Mapping snow algae in West Antarctic Peninsula from Sentinel-2 images using a machine learning based approach
record.abstract: Snow algae are crucial terrestrial carbon sinks and light-absorbing impurities in Antarctica. However, the distribution of snow algae across the West Antarctic Peninsula (WAP) remains poorly understood due to their high spatiotemporal variability and complex polar imaging conditions. This study develops a robust, large-scale mapping framework for green and red snow algae using machine learning. Our approach outperformed traditional spectral-index and spectral-unmixing methods across multiple challenging scenes, with the Kappa score improving from 0.51 and 0.49 to 0.82. By synthesizing 2676 Sentinel-2 images, the 2019–2024 composite distribution of WAP snow algae and the interannual variability of bloom intensity were assessed. Results reveal a total bloom area of 54.34 km2, and uncover significant negative association between bloom intensity and the Antarctic Oscillation index. This research establishes a novel, transferable tool for mapping snow algae in cryosphere systems and provides a baseline for evaluating their ecological implications in a changing climate.

record.title: A soybean mapping framework via multi-index-derived pseudo-label enhancement and contrastive embedding neural network
record.abstract: Soybean is one of the most important oilseed crops globally, serving as a key ingredient in soy-based foods, meat alternatives, and animal feed. Accurate and timely monitoring of its spatial distribution is critical for ensuring food security and promoting the formulation of mutually beneficial international trade policies. However, large-scale mapping continues to face two major practical challenges: (i) index-based methods exhibit limited transferability across regions and years due to their sensitivity to threshold setting, and (ii) classifier-based methods are constrained by the scarcity, high acquisition cost, and potential inaccuracy of training samples. We propose a fully label-free soybean mapping framework that combines multi-index pseudo-label generation and the Pseudo-label Enhanced Contrastive Embedding Network (PEACE-Net). Pseudo-labels are generated by applying a majority voting mechanism to three well-validated soybean indices (GWCCI, GWCCI2, and SMCI), which collectively capture a broad spectrum of discriminative features of soybean, with cross-validation implemented across the indices to enhance reliability. PEACE-Net is a dual-head Transformer architecture incorporating a soft probability update mechanism: (i) a contrastive head that constructs a discriminative embedding space, and (ii) a classification head whose soft outputs iteratively refine pseudo-labels, thereby progressively reducing the risk of overfitting under weak supervision. The framework was evaluated across five representative sites in the United States, Brazil, Argentina, and China from 2021 to 2024, and through three large-scale regional mapping experiments. Multi-index pseudo-labels demonstrated more accurate and stable performance than single-index labels. PEACE-Net outperformed baseline methods (RF, DCM, and Transformer) across sites and years, achieving an average OA of 90.72% and F1-score of 0.91, with balanced Precision and Recall. Large-scale regional mapping in three areas shows a strong linear correlation (R2 > 0.90) between mapped soybean area and county-level data, closely matching official records. These findings underscore the significant potential of the proposed framework for large-scale soybean mapping at both regional and global scales. By integrating the complementary strengths of index-based and classifier-based methods, the framework achieves fully automated, end-to-end, and label-free mapping with high efficiency and precision.

record.title: A semi-supervised deep learning framework based on multi-source data for wheat: from counting to yield estimation
record.abstract: Efficient quantification of wheat ears and spike grains is crucial for yield estimation but is currently hindered by the heavy reliance on labor-intensive manual annotations and complex field environments. There is also no unified approach for the simultaneous segmentation and counting of wheat ears and spike grains. To address these issues, this study proposed a semi-supervised deep learning framework for wheat. First, we constructed a Wheat Segment Anything Model (Wheat-SAM), which integrates adapters and is fine-tuned on a large-scale dataset of wheat ear and spike grain images to generate high-quality training samples. Subsequently, we developed the Wheat Segmentation and Counting U-Net (WSCU-Net), an innovative dual-task framework that combines Depthwise Separable Convolutions (DSConv) and Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA), enabling simultaneous segmentation and counting of wheat ears and spike grains. Specifically, we fine-tuned Wheat-SAM to generate pseudo labels, which were subsequently used to train WSCU-Net. The trained WSCU-Net was then employed to predict segmentation masks and count outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that the fine-tuned Wheat-SAM achieved the highest segmentation accuracy across multiple scales and maintained stable performance under different prompt modes, confirming its capability in generating high-quality pseudo annotations. Furthermore, the semi-supervised WSCU-Net trained on pseudo labels outperformed other dual-stage fusion methods in both segmentation and counting tasks, achieving an IoU of 0.8409 and a Coefficient of Determination (R2) of 0.766, approaching the performance of fully supervised models. Notably, WSCU-Net maintained robust performance across different wheat cultivars, highlighting its applicability in diverse field scenarios. Preliminary correlation analysis between the predicted count results and actual yield showed a strong positive statistical relationship, with an average Pearson correlation coefficient (r) of 0.6918. Our approach provides valuable insights into leveraging foundation models in wheat phenotyping tasks and holds great promises for intelligent wheat yield estimation. It offers strong support for wheat breeding, remote sensing yield prediction, and other smart agriculture applications.

record.title: A spherical-harmonic deep learning framework for generic tree morphology and species identification
record.abstract: Tree biodiversity is declining at an unprecedented pace, threatening forest ecosystems and their ecological functions. Reliable tree species identification is essential for monitoring biodiversity change and developing strategies to mitigate further losses; however, spectral intra-class variability, inter-class similarity, and the structural complexity of trees continue to hinder tree species identification by intelligent algorithms. Herein, we constructed a generalized framework from a transdisciplinary perspective to characterize tree morphology, based exclusively on LiDAR data for tree species identification. First, we devised multiple point cloud projection strategies and radial manifold-derived geometric features in spherical space to comprehensively depict tree morphogenesis. Second, we developed an innovative deep learning model based on spherical harmonics and the rotation group SO(3) to explore the structural commonalities for each tree species and identify tree species across mesoscale forest landscapes. By analysing point clouds of nearly 200,000 trees from 59 species, we demonstrated that our framework has the ability to capture the spatial clustering behaviour of foliage clumps, the uneven appearance of tree crowns, and the canopy architectures of diverse trees. Our framework achieved species identification overall accuracies of 85.42% on the Chinese dataset and 85.03% on the FOR-species20K dataset, surpassing state-of-the-art deep learning approaches by 5.19% and 5.02%, respectively. The results present the effectiveness of our framework as a robust tool for assessing forest diversity at both community and ecosystem levels and have the potential to be applied to larger geographical regions.

record.title: IRSD-DETR: A lightweight real-time detection transformer for infrared ship detection
record.abstract: Infrared ship detection (IRSD) plays an important role in many applications such as thermal remote sensing for maritime safety and surveillance. However, its detection performance often degrades due to small target size, insufficient feature extraction and complex background interference, leading to frequent false alarms and missed detections. In addition, existing detection transformer (DETR)-based models suffer from heavy network parameters and high computational complexity. To solve these issues, we propose a lightweight real-time detection transformer for IRSD, termed IRSD-DETR. Firstly, four lightweight wavelet-based transform blocks (WTBs) significantly decrease the network parameters and computational complexity while maintaining decent detection accuracy and enhancing the multi-scale representation of infrared (IR) ships. Secondly, within the effective hybrid encoder (EHE), the attention-based intra-scale feature interaction adaptive sparse self-attention (AIFI_ASSA) module effectively suppresses noisy interactions from irrelevant areas while retaining the most informative features of IR ships. The lightweight relative position enhanced self-attention mechanism (RPESAM) module expands the receptive field without introducing extra computational costs. The pinwheel-shaped convolution (PSConv) substitutes the standard convolution, significantly reducing the loss of fine details of IR ships. Lastly, the normalized Gaussian Wasserstein distance (NWD) further enhances the stability and accuracy of bounding box regression for IRSD. record.title: Large vision-language model knowledge guided multi-source urban land-use mapping: A case study of representative cities across six continents
record.abstract: Urban land-use maps provide critical insights into the functional structure and urbanization process of cities. While high-resolution remote sensing (HRS) images offer detailed information on ground objects, they are insufficient for comprehensive land-use analysis, as land-use patterns involve both natural and socio-economic factors. To address this, integrating HRS images with points of interest (POIs) reflecting human activities has become a common approach. However, variations in physical appearances and POI density across cities pose challenges for large-scale urban land-use mapping. In this study, a large vision-language model knowledge-guided multi-source feature learning framework for urban land-use mapping (VLM-LU) is proposed. By leveraging a large vision-language model (VLM), the framework generates captions robust to environmental changes. It incorporates a voting-based mechanism and rule-based refinement to mitigate VLM hallucinations. Additionally, a joint object-guided visual representation refinement (JGR) module is introduced to improve robustness against variations in urban landscapes by guiding the visual encoder to focus on key areas. A confidence-aware gating (CAG) module further enhances performance by weighting the relative importance of each modality to obtain an informative fused representation. Experimental results on the Multi-CUN dataset and representative cities across six continents demonstrate that the proposed VLM-LU framework significantly improves the generalizability and robustness of large-scale urban land-use mapping. In several study areas, the overall accuracy (OA) of VLM-LU exceeds state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods by more than 10%. Even with limited annotated samples, VLM-LU still performs well, demonstrating its potential practicality in large-scale land-use mapping. The source code is available at https://github.com/Rayoll/VLM-LU.

record.title: Make more pixels usable: A data-driven framework for customizable cloud and shadow processing in satellite imagery
record.abstract: Atmospheric interference, particularly cloud cover, remains a persistent challenge in the effective utilization of optical remote sensing imagery. Existing cloud processing methods either localize cloud positions or remove cloud interference but fail to adaptively process cloudy imagery, leading to substantial loss of valuable pixel information. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a data-driven framework for optimizing pixel utilization in satellite images. First, we proposed an adjustable cloud intensity index to quantify the interference of cloud and shadow, facilitating selective processing of different cloud pixels. Furthermore, a novel cloud simulation strategy was applied to Landsat-8 data, generating globally-distributed cloud samples and constructing the benchmark CloudL8-LC dataset. The CloudL8-LC dataset comprises over 5.2 billion pixels and has the widest coverage among the existing cloud datasets, and supports cloud detection, cloud removal, and adjustable cloud processing. Based on this dataset, we developed a single-image cloud intensity estimation network (SCIENet) equipped with a relevance-aware attention module (RAAM) and a gating-based channel-spatial feature pruner (GCSFP), both designed to accommodate the inherent variability of cloud formations. Once the cloud intensity index is predicted by SCIENet, the threshold can be flexibly adjusted to accommodate user-specific requirements, enabling customizable cloud and shadow processing within single imagery. Additionally, we introduced a suite of evaluation metrics to assess cloud-processing performance in terms of pixel quantity, quality, and practical utility. Extensive experiments demonstrated that the proposed cloud intensity index functions as a dynamic thresholding parameter for single-image cloud processing, enabling selective masking of highly contaminated pixels while reconstructing minimally affected regions. This provides users with tunable cloud processing solutions and exhibits robustness across diverse cloud types. Compared to cloud detection approaches, SCIENet significantly enhances pixel availability while maintaining reliable classification accuracy, ensuring consistent performance across various land-cover scenarios. Furthermore, in some real-world cloud conditions where the classic cFmask algorithm achieves a cloud detection precision below 70%, the proposed SCIENet model attains a precision of up to 90%. Additionally, relative to manually annotated masks, the SCIENet can increase the number of clear pixels by over 15%, making more pixels usable.

record.title: Unsupervised anomaly localization with high-resolution and time-series satellite imagery: from global disaster dataset to zero-shot model via SAM
record.abstract: The stable and balanced conditions of our living environment are upset by land surface disasters like earthquakes and floods, which frequently result in fatalities and wildly unpredictable damage. However, achieving generalizable damage localization for first-response humanitarian assistanc e poses significant challenges due to the diverse types of disaster scenes (e.g., urban, mountain, rural) and damaged objects (e.g., buildings, roads, croplands), none of which we can predict in advance. Most of existing studies are often limited to either certain disaster type or certain damage object type including both supervised and unsupervised models. To achieve a unified damage localization, we first propose a new unsupervised anomaly change detection paradigm for damage localization, which takes an arbitrary number of time steps and makes use of all previous images as a guide to differentiate between “anomaly changes” and “normal changes” brought on by sporadic human activity or changing imaging circumstances. This paradigm is motivated by the observation that catastrophic damages correlate with anomaly changes not seen in any historical image, without the need of any damage annotation and being damage-aware. We implement the paradigm as a zero-shot anomaly change detection model called AnomalyCD, which adapts the single-temporal foundation model (i.e., segment anything model (SAM)) for our task with designed feature-mask interaction. Proposed adaptation maps the segmented objects into feature space and conducts temporal comparison to calculate the change score with bi-temporal images and anomaly change score with all historical images. AnomalyCD is validated on the constructed global-scale dataset called GDL involving six disaster types and six damage types, which has multiple time steps (3–7), high resolution (0.15–2.39 m/pixel), and cover a large area (2052.82 km2 in total) collected globally. Without any training process, AnomalyCD have surpassed the best previous unsupervised methods by 7 points in F1 metric (from 42.66 to 50.27) and achieved comparable performance with supervised specialized models for certain damage type, emphasizing the ability of AnomalyCD to help national emergent agencies respond quickly to disasters. Code would be released at https://github.com/Jingtao-Li-CVer/AnomalyCD.

record.title: Annual wetland changes across China (2016–2024) from multisource temporal data and knowledge-driven machine learning approach
record.abstract: Timely and accurate data on wetland dynamics are crucial for effective conservation planning, policy implementation, and the achievement of sustainable development. However, obtaining high-resolution wetland change data at the national scale remains a significant challenge, with the lack of a comprehensive, long-term dataset for China. In this study, we present an enhanced wetland mapping framework that integrates multi-source temporal data with a prior knowledge-driven machine learning approach. By incorporating prior knowledge from the estimated probability of wetland occurrence, this method spatially constrains the potential distribution of wetlands, significantly boosting computational efficiency and reducing both misclassification and training data requirements. Leveraging over 2.59 million Sentinel images, we produced China’s annual 10-m resolution wetland change product for the period of 2016–2024, with an average overall accuracy of 81.72% (ranging from 80.55% to 82.17%). The results indicate that China’s total wetland area remained broadly stable from 2016 to 2024, with a marginal net gain of 0.5%. Water bodies showed the greatest interannual variability (1.23 × 103 km2) and expanded overall (+1.24%), while coastal swamps also increased slightly. By contrast, coastal marshes (−0.62 × 103 km2) and tidal flats (−0.71 × 103 km2) declined, inland marshes decreased marginally (−0.11%), and inland swamps exhibited no significant change. Regionally, the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau and Northeast China displayed the highest variability. This high-resolution, annually updated wetland dataset provides a critical resource for wetland conservation, restoration, and ecological management, and will play a pivotal role in supporting both national and global efforts to assess and achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

record.title: Uncertainty quantification framework for aerial and UAV photogrammetry through error propagation
record.abstract: Uncertainty quantification of the photogrammetry process is essential for providing per-point accuracy credentials of the point clouds. Unlike airborne LiDAR, whose accuracy generally remains consistent with objects with varying geometric complexity, the accuracy of photogrammetric point clouds is rather object/scene-dependent, as it relies on algorithm-derived measurements. Generally, errors of the photogrammetric point clouds propagate through a two-step process: Structure-from-Motion (SfM) with Bundle adjustment (BA), followed by Multi-view Stereo (MVS). While uncertainty estimation in the SfM stage has been well studied using the first-order statistics of the reprojection error function, that in the MVS stage remains largely unsolved and non-standardized, primarily due to its non-differentiable and multi-modal nature (i.e., from pixel values to geometry). In this paper, we present an uncertainty quantification framework closing this gap by associating an error covariance matrix per point accounting for this two-step photogrammetry process. Specifically, to estimate the uncertainty in the MVS stage, we propose a novel, self-calibrating method by taking reliable n-view points (n ≥ 6) per-view to regress the disparity uncertainty using highly relevant cues (such as matching cost values) from the MVS stage. Compared to existing approaches, our method uses self-contained, reliable 3D points extracted directly from the MVS process, with the benefit of being self-supervised and naturally adhering to error propagation path of the photogrammetry process, thereby providing a robust and certifiable uncertainty quantification across diverse scenes. We evaluate the framework using a variety of publicly available airborne and UAV imagery datasets. Results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches by achieving high bounding rates without overestimating uncertainty. More information, including test cases and sample datasets, can be found at: https://github.com/GDAOSU/UncertaintyQuantification.

record.title: An integrated machine learning approach for efficient gap-filling of cloudy Landsat LST imagery
record.abstract: Cloud contamination causes substantial gaps in Landsat land surface temperature (LST) records, limiting their spatiotemporal continuity amid growing demand for long-term high-resolution thermal data. Despite progress, gap-filling Landsat LST remains challenging due to large spatiotemporal gaps, realistic under-cloud representation, and multi-source discrepancies. To address these challenges simultaneously, this study proposes an integrated machine learning approach that combines complementary strengths of spatial reference-based fusion and temporal reference-based interpolation in a simple yet efficient way. Specifically, the cost-efficient Light Gradient Boosting Machine model is employed as a unified architecture, into which key factors are jointly incorporated: the adjacent Landsat image (LR) as a high-resolution spatial anchor, annual temperature cycle pattern (ATC) as a physically-guided temporal baseline, surface-energy-balance-guided all-weather thermal changes bridging large temporal gaps under cloudy conditions, and synchronous environmental variables facilitating adaptive adjustment over heterogeneous surfaces. The method was evaluated on both simulated and actual cloudy Landsat images during 2017–2021 across SURFRAD regions. Results show consistent recovery of spatially complete, high-resolution thermal patterns with RMSEs of 0.99 K (satellite-based) and 2.01 K (ground-based). The accuracies are comparable to clear-sky Landsat products, superior to GOES LST under cloudy conditions, and outperform four representative methods, reducing RMSEs by 1.23–2.72 K (satellite-based) and 0.58–3.94 K (ground-based). Impact analyses confirm robustness under varied cloud cover and temporal gaps. Model interpretation reveals that LR and ATC dominate the learning process, while others provide secondary refinements, supporting the rationale, interpretability, and generalizability of the proposed approach. This study facilitates the generation of continuous high-resolution thermal datasets for diverse applications.

record.title: TAIS-Net: Time adaptive implicit sampling diffusion model for arbitrary-scale UAV video super-resolution
record.abstract: Emerging applications urgently require unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) videos with high clarity and rich structural details. However, limitations in imaging sensors and non-ideal conditions often result in blurred videos lacking sufficient details. Recent studies indicate diffusion models have strong potential for natural scene video super-resolution (SR). However, the application of diffusion models to UAV video SR remains underexplored, particularly in the context of arbitrary-scale reconstruction. To tackle the challenges in UAV video SR at arbitrary scales, this work introduces a time adaptive implicit sampling diffusion model TAIS-Net. First, to achieve robust temporal alignment under large camera motions and texture scarcity commonly encountered in UAV videos, we use a reference frame alignment module to compensate previously reconstructed frames by incorporating motion cues estimated from a pre-trained optical flow model. Second, to enable scale-flexible reconstruction while preserving fine geometric details for UAV videos under arbitrary upscaling factors, we introduce an implicit denoising U-Net to learn latent features by leveraging implicit neural representations and a temporal conditioning module. Third, to reduce the prediction error propagation during sampling, we introduce a historical sample gain module that dynamically corrects and refines latent features at each sampling step, thereby suppressing temporal artifacts such as flickering or drifting. Finally, an arbitrary-scale implicit decoder is used to reconstruct high-resolution videos directly from these enhanced latent features, avoiding scale-dependent blurring while preserving high-frequency details in UAV videos. To validate the effectiveness of TAIS-Net, we construct two visible and one infrared UAV video SR datasets. The experimental results on these datasets demonstrate that TAIS-Net attains competitive performance relative to existing methods in terms of reconstruction quality, perceptual quality and temporal consistency. Moreover, experiments on various motion intensities and additional Gaussian blur beyond conventional bicubic downsampling degradation without requiring model retraining also demonstrate the superiority of our TAIS-Net in maintaining perceptual and temporal consistency under real-world UAV scenarios. The code and datasets are available at https://github.com/cyber-lwk/TAIS-Net.

record.title: Shallow-water reef detection driven by few-shot learning with airborne LiDAR bathymetry
record.abstract: Shallow-water reefs play an important scientific and practical role in ensuring navigational safety and supporting marine aquaculture. However, traditional detection methods such as shipborne sonar and multibeam echo sounding face significant challenges in achieving high-precision detection. These challenges stem from complex reef morphology and grounding risks associated with unmanned surface vehicles. In contrast, airborne LiDAR bathymetry (ALB) provides an effective alternative, enabling non-contact, high-accuracy measurements over broad spatial extents. This study proposes a few-shot learning–based detection method using ALB data. It addresses challenges posed by large morphological variability and limited training samples in shallow-water reef detection. We developed upon an enhanced You Only Look Once version 10 (YOLOv10) framework, incorporating a Cross-Scale Attention Module (CSAM) to strengthen feature perception and representation. Moreover, a joint training strategy is employed to enhance model adaptability. This strategy integrates data augmentation with meta-learning to ensure robustness under few-shot scenarios. The proposed approach was validated using ALB data collected over Jiaozhou Bay, Qingdao, China. Experimental results under few-shot conditions (10 samples) show that the proposed method achieves a precision of 97.9% and a recall of 98.4%, demonstrating superior detection accuracy and stability compared with existing algorithms. These findings establish a reliable technical foundation for high-precision shallow-water reef detection in marine engineering and environmental monitoring applications. For benchmarking and reproducibility purposes, the constructed ReefFeat-Img dataset and the source code of the proposed method are publicly available at: https://github.com/biguanglu350/FSAM-YOLO.git.

record.title: Sparse multimodal feature fusion transformer with frequency-convolution collaboration for wildlife multi-object tracking in UAV monitoring
record.abstract: Lightweight unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are gradually becoming important remote sensing tools for wildlife monitoring. Wildlife tracking using UAVs faces challenges, including small targets, highly similar appearances, and strong camouflage in natural environments. To address these issues, we propose a multimodal wildlife multi-object tracking model based on text–image feature fusion. First, the Density Multimodal Fusion (DTF) module combines spatial-density-guided sparse sampling with text priors to focus on high-density foregrounds while suppressing background redundancy. Second, the frequency-convolution collaborative encoder (LST-Encoder) performs spatially conditioned spectral modulation to enhance informative frequency components and preserve global semantics, improving discriminability for camouflaged and visually similar targets. Finally, the Hybrid-Decoder mitigates ID switches and identity fragmentation by integrating global spatiotemporal modeling with hierarchical identity modulation, maintaining cross-frame feature continuity and reinforcing identity-specific cues for stable long-sequence tracking. We validate our approach on the newly constructed MiluDrone dataset and public datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed method significantly outperforms several representative trackers, achieving a 4% increase in MOTA, a 3.7% increase in IDF1, and a 47% reduction in ID switches on the MiluDrone dataset. These results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed framework for challenging UAV-based wildlife monitoring scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/yzxhao123/De-MOTR.git.

record.title: Deviation-guided dual-model machine learning SAR coherence change detection framework for extracting changes in low-coherence areas
record.abstract: Coherence Change Detection (CCD) is a crucial technique for monitoring surface dynamics in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), and it has wide-ranging applications in natural disaster monitoring and urban analysis. However, conventional CCD methods based on dual-temporal coherence typically rely on a single coherence estimate for decision-making. This makes it difficult to effectively distinguish between decoherence caused by real surface changes and that induced by other factors, such as geometric decorrelation, temporal decorrelation, system noise, and co-registration inaccuracies. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel dual-model framework for coherence change detection that integrates machine learning with coherence and deviation modeling. The proposed framework first employs a machine learning (ML) model for coherence estimation, followed by a deviation prediction model that learns the mapping between statistical features and estimation errors. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method is then applied to interpret the deviation model. Based on the joint output of coherence and deviation estimates, a dual-threshold segmentation strategy is adopted to effectively extract low-coherence regions caused by genuine surface changes. Experimental results confirm the method’s robustness in small-sample and low-coherence scenarios. Validation with real-world data across different resolutions and scenarios confirms the method’s ability to accurately identify low-coherence regions caused by changes. By jointly utilizing coherence and deviation information, the proposed framework enhances detection accuracy and interpretability, providing a robust and reliable new CCD solution.

record.title: Multimodal deep learning with aerial imagery and nDSM for true-slope-aware rooftop photovoltaic potential estimation
record.abstract: Accurate assessment of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) potential is essential for renewable energy planning and carbon-neutral urban development. Most existing studies rely on a single data modality: aerial image-based methods often lack true-slope information, while three-dimensional (3D) building model-based methods usually omit roof superstructures and their impact on installable area. These limitations can introduce systematic errors and lead to biased PV potential estimates. To address these challenges, we propose SolarFusion, an innovative multimodal deep learning framework for high-precision, true-slope-aware rooftop PV potential assessment. SolarFusion combines semantic features from RGB aerial imagery with geometric-spatial attributes from normalized digital surface model (nDSM) data. At its core is the FusionPIRNet architecture, which integrates the cross-modal multi-scale feature integration (CMFI) module for adaptive coupling of heterogeneous data and the continual fusion optimization (CFO) module for progressive refinement of fused features. Two high-quality RGB-D benchmark datasets, RID1-Depth (0.10 m/pixel nDSM) and RID2-Depth (0.08 m/pixel nDSM), are constructed to enable robust evaluation and introduce true-slope awareness into rooftop PV analysis. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SolarFusion outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal fusion methods in both rooftop parsing and PV potential estimation. In particular, SolarFusion achieves the lowest estimation error, reducing the annual solar potential estimation error by at least 98.85 MWh/year on RID1-Depth and 44.61 MWh/year on RID2-Depth. A city-wide case study in Munich, Germany (374 km2) further highlights the framework’s scalability, identifying an annual generation potential of 3.2 TWh and successfully handling diverse urban morphologies, including high-density districts with complex rooftop configurations.

record.title: Towards comprehensive multi-task land cover change detection leveraging vision-language model and LLM-driven agents
record.abstract: Land cover change detection is essential for assessing the impacts of urbanization on ecological systems and economic development. As urbanization accelerates, land cover changes involve both semantic transitions and structural modifications, substantially increasing the complexity of detection tasks. However, existing research has primarily focused on 2D change detection, with limited integration of multi-dimensional and multi-modal data. This limitation has restricted the effective modeling of inter-class transitions and spatial structural evolution. Moreover, most methods lack end-to-end pipelines adapted to real-world scenarios, constraining their capacity for comprehensive representation and quantitative impact assessment. To address these challenges, we introduce UrbanChange, the first dataset designed for multi-task (2D and 3D) land cover change detection. It integrates semantic and structural change maps from multi-sensor data with fine-grained change captions, providing a comprehensive foundation for evaluating and analyzing land cover transformations. Leveraging UrbanChange, we develop a vision–language model that directly infers multi-dimensional changes from optical imagery. We further develop GaiaAgent by incorporating this model as a core perception module, forming the agentic workflow for land cover change detection and analysis. GaiaAgent coordinates five task-specific agents in an automated pipeline for instruction interpretation, task decomposition, detection, and quantitative analysis. A Human-in-the-Loop mechanism is incorporated to produce interactive, interpretable reports, enhancing robustness in complex scenarios. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of GaiaAgent. On the UrbanChange dataset, GaiaAgent achieves a 3.9% improvement in F1 and a 0.35 m reduction in cRMSE compared with the strongest baseline. In downstream applications across multiple analytical scenarios, GaiaAgent demonstrates improved reliability and adaptability in land cover change detection and interpretation.

record.title: Hemispheric-scale mapping of thaw slumps using a cloud-native and transferable deep learning framework
record.abstract: Accelerating permafrost degradation is driving the rapid expansion of thaw slumps (TS) across the Northern Hemisphere, posing increasing risks to ecosystems, infrastructure, and the global carbon cycle. However, reliable TS identification at continental to hemispheric scales remains challenging due to strong environmental heterogeneity, fragmented remote sensing workflows, and limited cross-regional transferability of existing methods. Here, we address the cross-regional transferability gap in hemispheric TS identification by developing a reproducible framework that couples cloud-native multi-source data fusion in Google Earth Engine (GEE) with a modular PyTorch-based deep learning pipeline. The framework operationalizes transferability through three coordinated components: (1) a physically interpretable channel design that integrates Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and topographic data to encode TS-relevant processes; (2) a structure-preserving feature representation using PCA-guided dimensionality reduction and SNIC-based superpixel segmentation to suppress noise while maintaining geomorphic consistency; and (3) a standardized cross-regional training and ablation strategy that identifies model configurations maximizing generalization rather than region-specific accuracy. Evaluations across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), the Arctic, and the broader Northern Hemisphere demonstrate that late-summer observations and fused optical–SAR channels consistently outperform single-sensor inputs. The LinkNet-EfficientNet-B7 configuration achieves intersection-over-union (IOU) scores of 0.802 in the QTP, 0.770 in the Arctic, and 0.776 at hemispheric scale. Cross-regional transfer experiments further confirm robust generalization, with the hemispheric model maintaining IOU values exceeding 0.63 across distinct permafrost domains without region-specific retraining. These results indicate that transferable TS mapping is not primarily determined by model complexity, but by the consistency between process-informed feature representation and cross-regional training design. The proposed GEE-PyTorch framework provides a computationally efficient and reproducible foundation for operational monitoring of thaw-induced geomorphic disturbances.

record.title: Rectify-Match-Reconstruct (RMR): Framework for dense and accurate metric 3D reconstruction via neural homography alignment
record.abstract: Accurate digital representations of civil infrastructure are essential for damage prognostics, condition assessment, and remaining-life prediction. While LiDAR-based sensing can generate dense geometric models, high deployment cost and extensive post-processing limit widespread use. Image-based photogrammetry offers a scalable alternative but struggles with scale ambiguity, unreliable feature correspondence, and degraded performance under wide baselines, repetitive textures, and geometric misalignment. These limitations significantly reduce the accuracy of dense metric 3D reconstruction required for structural assessment. This paper formulates a rectify-match-reconstruct (RMR) framework for generating dense, metrically accurate 3D reconstructions from field image collections. The method is built on the key insight that correspondence errors arise primarily from severe geometric misalignment between image pairs. To address this, a self-supervised, patch-wise neural homography alignment network is developed to geometrically rectify local image regions prior to dense matching. An iterative refinement process progressively improves alignment, enabling dense correspondence estimation to operate in a stable regime even under wide-baseline viewpoints and nonplanar scene geometry. The resulting correspondences are mapped back to the original images and combined with camera calibration referenced to the Building Information Model (BIM) to achieve dense metrically consistent 3D reconstructions. Extensive validation across structures of varying scale, texture, and viewpoint separation demonstrates that RMR brings over 90% reduction in correspondence error relative to state-of-the-art optical flow methods. The framework also enables self-supervised fine-tuning of dense matching models using field imagery, further improving reconstruction accuracy. By reframing homography as a geometric preconditioning mechanism, the proposed approach provides a practical and scalable pathway toward reliable, low-cost digital twin generation and automated structural condition assessment. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tmatiki2/RMR.

record.title: T2Net: Taxonomy-Guided Tree-Structured Prompt Learning for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification
record.abstract: Remote sensing image scene classification has long faced two major challenges: high inter-class similarity and significant intra-class variation, which limit the generalization ability of Vision Language Models (VLMs) in few-shot remote sensing scene classification tasks. Existing approaches leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate additional textual descriptions, but these unstructured and generic descriptions fail to effectively address these challenges at the semantic level in complex remote sensing scenes, where rich spatial layouts and complex land-cover distributions further exacerbate intra- and inter-class variations. To address this issue, we propose Taxonomy-Guided Tree-Structured Prompt Learning for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification (T2Net). Specifically, we first introduce the Taxonomic Knowledge Generation (TKG) module, which guides LLMs to construct tree-structured semantic representations using taxonomic knowledge. The generated root- and child-level semantics are then incorporated into prompt templates via different connectives. Root nodes define macro-level semantic boundaries to enhance inter-class separability, while child nodes capture shared intra-class characteristics to reduce intra-class variation. Furthermore, we introduce a bidirectional Taxonomic Knowledge Interaction (TKI) module to enable cross-modal exchange of taxonomic knowledge. Finally, we align taxonomic-aware features with learnable prompt representations to prevent semantic drift during training. Experiments across eight public datasets demonstrate that our T2Net outperforms existing methods.

record.title: Integrating physical modeling and data-driven learning: A DCNN for InSAR phase filtering and applications
record.abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) phase filtering is crucial for stable phase unwrapping and accurate topographic mapping and deformation retrieval. However, conventional spatial, frequency, and nonlocal filters, as well as existing learning-based methods, often struggle to balance noise suppression and detail preservation, especially under extremely low coherence and high fringe density, where oversmoothing and artifacts are prone to occur. This paper proposes InSAR-Net, a deep neural network for phase filtering targeting severely noisy InSAR scenarios. The network is trained on a high-fidelity physics-based synthetic dataset that spans a wide range of coherence levels, fringe densities, and deformation patterns, with enriched extremely low-coherence samples to improve robustness. InSAR-Net integrates Feature Separation Coding (FSC) to enhance phase-related physical representations, residual dense encoding with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) for multi-scale modeling, and Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) with phase consistency loss to suppress pseudo fringes while preserving edges and fine structures. Experiments on simulated and real SAR datasets demonstrate that InSAR-Net achieves superior performance over representative SOTA methods in terms of RMSE, PSNR, and SSIM, with more pronounced gains under strong noise conditions. Further validation using low-coherence masking, detrended residual phase analysis, and unwrapped phase stability assessment shows that InSAR-Net reduces random phase fluctuations and scattering-related noise in valid coherent areas, improves phase unwrapping reliability, and avoids physical interpretation of signal-void regions. The dataset and trained model will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/yangwangyangzi48/InSAR-Net.git.

record.title: SyneFloor: Synergizing zero-shot geometric priors and active learning for weakly supervised floorplan reconstruction
record.abstract: Indoor floorplan reconstruction from 3D point clouds is a fundamental task for digital twin and architectural modeling. However, fully supervised approaches heavily rely on exhaustive polygon-level annotations, which are notoriously time-consuming and labor-intensive to acquire. To address this bottleneck, we propose SyneFloor, a weakly supervised framework that achieves accurate floorplan reconstruction under extreme label scarcity. First, to overcome the structural degradation caused by sparse supervision, we extract robust instance-aware structural priors by leveraging the zero-shot segmentation capabilities of vision foundation models (e.g., SAM3). We then propose an Adaptive Mask-Query Synergistic Fusion (AMQSF) module to dynamically fuse these explicit geometric priors into Transformer queries. Second, to maximize the data efficiency of the limited annotation budget, we design a stage-wise, multi-criteria active learning strategy. By comprehensively evaluating predictive uncertainty and architectural complexity, the model actively selects the most informative and challenging scenes for annotation. Third, to fully exploit the remaining unannotated data, we introduce a topology-aware pseudo-label generation mechanism within a dual-network collaborative framework. By explicitly detecting and resolving topological conflicts, this mechanism produces high-quality, structurally valid pseudo-labels, which fundamentally guarantees the robustness of the semi-supervised learning process. Extensive experiments on the synthetic Structured3D and real-world SceneCAD datasets demonstrate the superiority of SyneFloor. It not only exhibits robustness by consistently outperforming current state-of-the-art methods under extreme label scarcity (1% to 10% budgets), but also matches or surpasses several 100% fully supervised methods with much less labeled expenditure (e.g. utilizing only 40% of labels). This dual capability thereby establishes a highly scalable and annotation-efficient paradigm for automated indoor floorplan reconstruction in practical applications.

record.title: Arctic sea ice motion retrieval via vision foundation model and cross-sensor SAR
record.abstract: Monitoring Arctic sea ice motion (SIM) is of critical importance for polar climate research. Although synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enables all weather observations, the relatively long revisit interval of a single sensor constrains the spatial and temporal extent of SIM monitoring. Cross-sensor SAR collaboration can overcome this limitation, yet it is challenged by pronounced nonlinear radiometric distortions (NRDs) and geometric distortions between images. To address these issues, this study proposes a vision foundation model-driven framework for cross-sensor SAR collaborative monitoring of Arctic SIM. First, a cross-sensor feature extraction module via the DINOv2 vision foundation model is developed to derive robust semantic features that mitigate NRDs. Second, a multi-scale optical flow estimation module with embedded SIM Physics is designed to alleviate geometric distortions. Experiments using Sentinel-1, ALOS-2, RCM, and C-SAR data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in vector retrieval under both summer and winter conditions. Comparisons with IABP buoy measurements indicate that the retrieved velocity RMSE is within 0.73 cm/s and the directional RMSE is within 4.6°. In addition, the proposed framework substantially enhances spatiotemporal coverage, increasing the average number of effective coverage days over the Arctic by 53% and the average effective coverage area by 75%. This work provides a new technical pathway toward large scale, high precision SIM monitoring across the entire Arctic.

record.title: Advancing hyperspectral nutrient modeling through transfer learning: Insights from foliar N–P–K estimation in cranberries
record.abstract: Efficient and accurate monitoring of crop nutrient status is essential for optimizing fertilization and promoting sustainable production. Hyperspectral remote sensing offers a promising approach for estimating foliar nutrient concentrations, yet the transferability of predictive models across different spatial, temporal, and plant domains remains a major challenge. In this study, we systematically evaluated the effectiveness of transfer learning techniques for improving the transferability of hyperspectral models in predicting cranberry foliar nitrogen (Nmass), phosphorus (Pmass), and potassium (Kmass) concentrations. We assessed four transfer scenarios: (1) across geographic locations (from NEON domains to a cranberry farm in Wisconsin); (2) across growth stages; (3) across leaf types; and (4) from PROSAIL-PRO–derived synthetic datasets to field-measured datasets. Four representative transfer learning approaches — transfer component analysis (TCA), transfer adaptive boosting for regression (TrAdaBoostR2), parameter regularization, and fine-tuning — were applied to partial least squares regression (PLSR) and deep neural network (DNN) models. Results showed that baseline models trained on source domains performed poorly when directly applied to target domains, with median normalized root-mean-square-errors (nRMSE) ranging from 16 to 71 % across scenarios. Transfer learning substantially improved model performance and reduced prediction uncertainty, with parameter regularization and TrAdaBoostR2 generally outperforming TCA. Model transferability varied with nutrient type: Nmass exhibited higher temporal variability and greater distributional shifts, whereas Pmass and Kmass were more reliably predicted due to their indirect spectral correlations. Fine-tuning the DNN on as little as 10–30 % of target-domain data achieved significant improvements, highlighting the efficiency of hybrid transfer learning. Our findings provide practical insights into selecting effective transfer learning strategies for hyperspectral nutrient mapping and demonstrate the feasibility of scaling nutrient monitoring across diverse crop systems, growth stages, and leaf types.
